Business goal: Read a paginated summary catalog of persisted backend capability records with normalized contract and access metadata so existing backend seams can be searched selected and reused safely by future frontend composition tooling.
User outcome: A privileged root operator or internal planning tool can browse search and filter which feature capabilities exist what request and response bodies they expose and which governing roles and authz capabilities apply from one durable catalog seam for use in menus drawers and hierarchy-style pickers.
Notes / constraints: The capability is the primary catalog unit, not the route or entity. V1 should cover approved HTTP-backed public feature capabilities first. Access truth is canonical in governing authz capability keys; role visibility is a persisted derived view produced by the normalization pipeline from maintained role-mapping artifacts. Read paths should use persisted catalog records, not live route-handler scraping. Summary rows should be selection-friendly and support grouping by feature route family seam type or lifecycle posture.
Tenant context rule: root-operated planning capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies in v1
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may browse the catalog in v1 because the catalog exposes protected backend capability truth intended for internal planning and future frontend-builder workflows.
Frontend visibility rule: Future builder and admin tooling should omit catalog surfaces when the current actor lacks the governing catalog-read capability. The catalog may later expose per-capability visibility hints and required runtime context filters but must not become the source of truth for authorization.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before list reads. Feature logic must read only persisted normalized records that were produced through the approved normalization pipeline and must surface stale or drifted catalog posture honestly.
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Client-side permission behavior: No client-side behavior in v1 beyond hiding or disabling future catalog UI when the actor lacks catalog-read permission.
Request contract: Query supports explicit filters only, such as `featureName`, `routeFamily`, `seamType`, `capabilityBoundary`, `governingAuthzCapability`, `allowedRole`, `catalogStatus`, `driftStatus`, `supportsRequestBody`, `supportsResponseFields`, `selectionGroup`, `page`, `pageSize`, and `orderDirection`. Optional exact-match and prefix-search fields such as `capabilityId`, `displayLabel`, or `featureNamePrefix` may be supported for picker-style discovery if they stay deterministic. No vague free-text blob search in v1.
Response contract: Returns paginated capability-summary rows from persisted catalog records with `featureName`, `capabilityId`, display label, route-family or grouping metadata, seam type, route metadata, contract coverage summary, governing authz capability keys, resolved allowed roles, required runtime context hints, catalog freshness, lifecycle flags, and picker-friendly selection metadata. Summary rows should indicate whether exact request and response field detail is available through the exact-read capability and should be usable as menu drawer or tree selection items without fetching full detail first.
Error contract: 400 invalid filter search selector or unsupported grouping mode; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 not found only when exact feature scoping requires it; 409 catalog drift or stale-materialization posture prevents an honest result when the requested view requires up-to-date truth.
Cross-feature seams: Consumes persisted normalized catalog records generated from approved feature-contract seams permission mappings feature manifests and API contract artifacts. Drift-audit tooling may compare persisted truth against current source artifacts but read paths should not depend on live source scanning.
Persistence impact: Read one durable capability-catalog record set plus supporting freshness drift and selection metadata. V1 should persist normalized records and allow later derived export without making exports authoritative.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique capability id within the catalog. Index on `(featureName, capabilityId)`. Index on route-family or selection-group metadata if those groupings are persisted. Index on governing authz capability. Index on drift status and freshness posture. Deterministic ordering by feature and capability id is required.
Search / filter model: Filter by explicit scalar fields only. Support deterministic picker search and grouping selectors rather than a generic search blob. Later UI-specific ranking rules should be explicit if introduced.
Compatibility / migration notes: The initial migration may seed the catalog from normalization output. Later feature-loop changes should refresh persisted records through the same pipeline and audit drift rather than silently tolerating stale catalog truth. Grouping and selection metadata should be stable enough for drawers trees and menu pickers to depend on them.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus central root authorization capability enforcement and feature-local freshness and drift guards.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct browser impact in API-only v1.
Audit requirement: Audit denied list access and consider auditing successful internal planning reads if repo audit posture treats contract inspection as security-relevant.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low to moderate; records may include internal field names and access metadata but should not expose secrets or raw credential material.
Standards impact: High anti-drift and integrity relevance because this feature becomes an input to later autonomous frontend-composition workflows and depends on governed refresh discipline.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged root operator can browse and select persisted backend capability records through honest filtered picker-friendly summaries with freshness posture and drift visibility, without the runtime feature inventing missing details from live source scraping.

Business goal: Read one exact persisted capability record with normalized request and response field paths plus static access metadata so frontend builders can bind UI elements to backend capability truth at field level.
User outcome: A privileged root operator or future internal builder can inspect one backend capability in detail including request params query body response fields role posture governing authz capability keys and future runtime-context hooks for omission filters from one persisted catalog record.
Notes / constraints: Exact reads should return field-level paths such as `params.id`, `query.page`, `body.email`, and `response.items[].status`. V1 should include required/optional, type, enum, format, repeated, and nullable metadata where the normalization pipeline can support it honestly. V1 should also persist required runtime-context hints such as `currentTenantId` or `subjectEntityId` when the backend contract already implies them, but must not implement dynamic omission logic yet.
Tenant context rule: root-operated planning capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies in v1
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may inspect exact catalog entries in v1 because exact records expose field-level contract structure and access posture intended for internal planning and frontend composition.
Authz scope type: exact read over one capability record
Frontend visibility rule: Future builder tooling should hide exact capability detail when catalog-read permission is absent and should treat field-level access metadata as advisory mirror data rather than client-side authority.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before exact reads. Feature logic must resolve one persisted capability record deterministically and must fail honestly when the catalog is stale incomplete or flagged as drifted beyond the allowed read posture.
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Client-side permission behavior: No client-side behavior in v1 beyond future internal UI gating based on catalog-read permission.
Request contract: Path requires one exact durable capability id or one deterministic feature-qualified identifier. No optional exact params. Request accepts no mutable body in v1.
Response contract: Returns one normalized persisted capability record containing feature identity seam metadata request contract partitions response contract fields access block resolved role mappings future runtime-context requirements source references freshness markers and compatibility notes. Field rows include stable paths binding hints and whether the field is system-managed or client-supplied.
Error contract: 400 invalid capability identifier shape; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 capability record not found; 409 stale or contradictory catalog posture prevents an honest exact record.
Cross-feature seams: Consumes persisted normalized catalog records produced by the normalization pipeline. Drift-audit tooling compares current source artifacts to persisted records but exact-read traffic should not reconstruct the record from source files at request time.
Persistence impact: Read one durable normalized capability-catalog row plus related field rows and access metadata. V1 should persist exact-record detail rather than deriving it on every request.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique durable capability ids must be deterministic across refresh runs. Index on capability id and feature-qualified selectors.
Search / filter model: Exact read only by capability id in v1. Secondary exact selectors should be deferred unless their stability is proven.
Compatibility / migration notes: Do not silently collapse multiple route variants or role variants into one vague exact record. Preserve stable identifiers explicit freshness posture and source references so future consumers can tell what is authoritative and what requires a refresh.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus central root authorization capability enforcement and feature-local freshness and drift guards.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct browser impact in API-only v1.
Audit requirement: Audit denied exact-read access and consider auditing successful exact record reads if internal contract inspection is classified as privileged planning activity.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; exact records may expose internal contract field names and access posture but must never surface secret values transient tokens or proof material.
Standards impact: High integrity and anti-drift relevance because exact field paths may later drive generated or semi-generated frontend slices.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged root operator can retrieve one persisted field-level capability record whose request response and access metadata are deterministic honest and refreshable through the governed normalization pipeline.

Business goal: Export a deterministic derived snapshot from persisted catalog records for downstream planning and frontend-builder tooling without making the export itself the durable source of truth.
User outcome: A privileged root operator or internal tool can retrieve a machine-usable snapshot of backend capability records for offline analysis builder initialization or later vertical-slice composition workflows from the persisted catalog layer.
Notes / constraints: Exports are derived outputs, not durable truth. The export must carry an explicit format version and freshness posture. Default exports should cover active approved HTTP-backed capabilities only. Later contextual omission filters may extend the exported schema with required runtime-context declarations, but v1 should not claim to evaluate those rules. Export evolution should happen through explicit format-version changes, not silent field churn.
Tenant context rule: root-operated planning capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies in v1
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may export the catalog in v1 because the export is intended for internal planning and builder-tooling workflows and may reveal broad capability coverage across the platform.
Authz scope type: root-scoped export over selected catalog scope
Frontend visibility rule: Future tooling should omit export actions when export permission is absent and should treat the exported snapshot as cacheable derived data rather than live authority.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before export. Feature logic must produce deterministic ordering explicit export-format versioning and explicit freshness and drift markers and must reject unsupported export scopes or target formats.
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Client-side permission behavior: No client-side behavior in v1 beyond future internal tooling gating based on export permission.
Request contract: Body selects scope and format explicitly, such as active features only optional feature allow-list requested export format version and whether stale-but-readable catalog rows are acceptable. No hidden ambient export scope.
Response contract: Returns a deterministic derived snapshot or artifact reference containing ordered capability records field metadata access blocks resolved role mappings runtime-context hints source references freshness posture drift markers and export-format version metadata while clearly labeling the output as derived.
Error contract: 400 invalid export scope or format version; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 referenced scope target not found when exact feature selection is used; 409 export blocked by drift or stale catalog posture that exceeds the caller's requested tolerance.
Cross-feature seams: Consumes persisted normalized catalog records and should be the preferred downstream machine-consumption seam instead of private source-file scraping or direct table access. The normalization pipeline remains responsible for keeping persisted records aligned with feature-source truth.
Persistence impact: Read-only derived export generation from persisted records in v1. Export snapshots are not themselves authoritative catalog records unless a later approved slice adds durable export history explicitly.
Indexes / uniqueness: Deterministic ordering and explicit export-format versioning are required. Indexes on catalog freshness and lifecycle posture should support predictable export scoping if the dataset grows.
Search / filter model: Export by explicit scope only. Avoid ambiguous partial export selectors in v1.
Compatibility / migration notes: Persisted catalog truth and derived export truth must stay separate. The initial migration may seed catalog rows from normalization output
Authentication requirement: and later refresh runs should update persisted rows before export consumers depend on them.
CSP / browser security impact: Root auth middleware plus central root authorization capability enforcement and feature-local export-scope validation.
Audit requirement: No direct browser impact in API-only v1.
Privacy / personal data impact: Audit successful and denied export attempts if internal catalog export is treated as privileged planning activity.
Standards impact: Moderate; exports may include broad internal capability metadata and access posture but must exclude secrets credentials and raw security proof material.
PRD required?: High integrity and anti-drift relevance because this export may become the seed input for later semi-automated frontend composition workflows.
column65: Capability is acceptable when a privileged root operator can export a stable machine-usable snapshot from persisted catalog records with explicit format versioning honest freshness posture and no confusion between derived export data and authoritative catalog storage.

Business goal: Normalize approved feature-source truth into persisted capability-catalog records so runtime reads and exports depend on one durable catalog seam instead of scattered live source interpretation.
User outcome: A governed feature-loop or privileged maintenance flow can refresh persisted capability records after a feature seam changes so later frontend and planning consumers read stable normalized truth.
Notes / constraints: This is a materialization capability, not a user-facing CRUD workflow. The normalization pipeline should read approved feature contracts permission mappings manifests and maintained contract artifacts, produce deterministic normalized records, and write them into durable catalog storage. The same normalization logic should be usable both for initial seeding and later refresh. Treat this as governed platform maintenance, not ad hoc manual editing of catalog rows.
Tenant context rule: root-operated maintenance flow outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies in v1
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability; direct client mutation of catalog rows
Authorization summary: Only governed maintenance flows may materialize catalog records because this capability defines the durable bridge between backend source truth and frontend-consumable catalog truth.
Authz scope type: maintenance execution over selected feature scope
Frontend visibility rule: No frontend visibility in v1. Future admin tooling may expose refresh posture
Backend enforcement rule: but direct catalog mutation should remain tightly controlled and not treated as normal application UI.
Audit actor role required?: Materialization must run through approved pipeline inputs and validation. It must reject contradictory or incomplete source truth rather than silently synthesizing records. Normal callers must not mutate persisted catalog rows directly.
Client-side permission behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules for any manual maintenance trigger. Automated feature-loop execution may run through internal maintenance or migration context instead of an end-user session.
Request contract: POST /v1/capability-contract-catalog/materialize or internal non-HTTP pipeline seam if the repo decides this should remain support-only in v1
Response contract: Request selects feature scope refresh mode and whether drifted rows may be overwritten after validation. Internal pipeline executions may use a non-HTTP seam with equivalent scoped inputs.
Error contract: Returns materialization summary including refreshed capability count skipped rows source-validation issues resulting freshness posture and whether any records remain drifted or blocked.
Feature seam(s): 400 invalid scope or refresh mode; 401 unauthenticated for manual triggers; 403 unauthorized; 409 contradictory source truth drift block or attempted overwrite without approved mode; 422 normalization validation failed.
Persistence impact: Consumes approved feature-contract seams permission mappings feature manifests maintained API contracts and later approved generated contract metadata. Should not read private feature persistence directly. Initial migration seeding may call the same normalization logic or consume its generated seed artifact.
Migration required?: Insert and update durable catalog rows field rows access rows source-reference rows and freshness metadata. This is the first write path for the feature and establishes the persisted registry.
Search / filter model: Unique constraints on capability id field path rows and source-reference rows. Index on feature name lifecycle freshness and last materialized timestamp.
Session / auth dependency: Materialization scope should be explicit by feature set or approved global refresh only. No vague search-driven refresh in v1.
Compatibility / migration notes: Authenticated root session required for manual operator triggers. Automated migration or feature-loop execution may use an internal maintenance context.
Authentication requirement: Initial seeding may happen through migration-backed import from normalization output. Later seam changes should update records through the same governed pipeline rather than hand-editing durable rows or relying on runtime derivation.
Authorization enforcement layer: Authenticated root session for manual operator triggers or approved internal maintenance context for automated runs.
CSP / browser security impact: Central root authorization for manual triggers plus feature-local normalization validation and persistence guards.
Audit requirement: No direct browser impact in API-only v1.
Privacy / personal data impact: Audit materialization runs especially when they overwrite persisted records or surface source drift blocking deployment readiness.
Standards impact: Moderate; source references and normalized contract metadata may expose internal implementation shape but should never include secret values or raw credential material.
PRD required?: Very high anti-drift relevance because this write path governs whether the persisted catalog remains trustworthy.
column65: Capability is acceptable when the approved normalization pipeline can seed and refresh durable capability-catalog records deterministically and refuse to persist ambiguous backend truth.

Business goal: Compare persisted catalog records against current approved feature-source truth so stale or inconsistent capability records are visible and can be repaired before frontend tooling relies on them.
User outcome: A privileged root operator or governed feature-loop can see whether persisted capability records have drifted from current backend truth and what needs rematerialization.
Notes / constraints: The drift audit should reuse the normalization pipeline's comparison logic. It should classify rows as in-sync stale drifted blocked or missing and should explain which source artifacts disagree. This capability should support feature-loop enforcement and honest runtime freshness posture, not best-effort silent repair.
Tenant context rule: root-operated planning and maintenance capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies in v1
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators or governed maintenance flows may inspect detailed drift posture because it exposes internal platform consistency gaps.
Frontend visibility rule: No frontend surface in v1 beyond possible future admin visibility of high-level drift posture. Builder tooling should consume freshness markers from persisted records rather than running source comparisons itself.
Backend enforcement rule: Drift audit must compare current approved source artifacts against persisted records using the same normalization rules as materialization. It must not mutate persisted rows unless a separate approved materialization action is invoked.
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules for manual audit reads. Automated feature-loop execution may run in an internal maintenance context.
Route(s): GET /v1/capability-contract-catalog/drift or internal non-HTTP audit seam if the repo decides support-only execution is sufficient in v1
Request contract: Query supports explicit feature scope lifecycle status and drift classification filters. Internal pipeline execution may use an equivalent non-HTTP seam.
Response contract: Returns drift summary and per-capability findings including current persisted freshness, source mismatch classes, missing rows, blocked normalization issues, and whether rematerialization is recommended or required.
Error contract: 400 invalid scope or filter; 401 unauthenticated for manual audit calls; 403 unauthorized; 409 source-truth resolution blocked by contradictory artifacts when the audit cannot classify honestly.
Cross-feature seams: Consumes the same approved source artifacts and persisted catalog records as materialization. Should integrate with feature-loop governance and later CI or standards checks where appropriate.
Persistence impact: Read-only audit over durable catalog rows and current source truth. Stores optional last-audited timestamps and findings only if a later slice approves durable audit history.
Indexes / uniqueness: Index on drift status feature name and last audited timestamp if durable audit metadata is added in v1; otherwise rely on catalog freshness indexes and deterministic comparison order.
Search / filter model: Filter by explicit scalar drift status and feature scope only.
Session / auth dependency: Authenticated root session required for manual audit access or approved internal maintenance context for automated runs.
Compatibility / migration notes: Drift should be surfaced honestly during feature loops rather than discovered only at runtime by frontend consumers. This capability is part of the governance model for keeping the persisted registry trustworthy.
Authentication requirement: Authenticated root session for manual audit access or approved internal maintenance context for automated runs.
Authorization enforcement layer: Central root authorization for manual audit access plus feature-local comparison validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct browser impact in API-only v1.
Audit requirement: Audit denied drift-inspection requests and consider audit visibility for remediation-triggering drift findings if repo policy treats catalog health as operationally significant.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low to moderate; drift findings reveal internal consistency gaps but should not expose secret values.
Standards impact: Very high anti-drift relevance because this is the explicit audit seam that keeps the persisted registry honest.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when operators and governed feature loops can detect stale or drifted capability-catalog records before downstream tooling treats them as trustworthy source material.
